clue.text: I can upset a clergy-man — but it's not right

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense, upset means overturned, so the word can is turned back to front

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman in a parish

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they might knock over a priest, admitting that would be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' works in a down-reading sense, turning the word backwards; 'a' is only a link before the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong or erroneous is incorrect, lacking precision or truth.

clue.text: Article about Kipling poem of unaffected simplicity

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
If— is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem of advice to a son

explanation.surface: An essay discusses a Kipling poem praised for its plain, artless style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the article backwards; If— is the Kipling poem of advice beginning 'If you can keep your head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A naive or ingenuous person or manner shows artless, innocent simplicity.

clue.text: A French wine cartel broken up

indicators.note: a cartel being broken up suggests its letters are split and regrouped in a new order

explanation.surface: A business cartel controlling French wine is dismantled by regulators.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, a French red wine.

clue.text: Modernises tap used irregularly

indicators.note: irregularly suggests the letters of tap and used are placed out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone renovates a tap that is only used now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To modernise something is to bring it up to date with current versions.

clue.text: Help's about run dry

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for help goes around the letter for run

parts.note: aid means help; the 's stands for is and links nothing extra
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Assistance arrives just as supplies run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AID around R; the 's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is parched, lacking moisture.

clue.text: Healey's unusual facial hair!

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of Healey's come out in an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man named Healey sports strange growth on his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges all seven letters of HEALEYS, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Each lash fringing the eyelid is a small hair on the face.

clue.text: Excellent example of rudimentary instruction

explanation.surface: A beginner's lesson is praised as outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: the very first class a pupil attends is the most basic teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-grade means superb; and an opening lesson is the most elementary teaching a pupil gets.

clue.text: A comfortable place in the garden

definitions.text: A comfortable place in the garden

parts.words: A comfortable place in the garden
parts.note: an idiom for an easy, pleasant situation, pictured literally as a flower bed planted with a favourite bloom

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a life of ease, and literally names a planted area of rose bushes.

clue.text: The bird is flown

explanation.surface: A bird of prey soars through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hawk-like raptor, and also a toy on a string that children fly on windy days.

clue.text: Dining out with meal and drink

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of dining and meal are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Eating out, a diner orders food and something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINING plus MEAL; 'with' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of spirit and lime cordial is a mixed beverage.

clue.text: Dismisses a proposal to start moving

explanation.surface: A boss sends staff away and urges everyone to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who releases or sacks a person frees them; and the phrase is a call for a group to set off together.

clue.text: Being more bulky, puts out the fire

indicators.note: puts out suggests the letters of the fire are disturbed and set out anew

explanation.surface: A big, burly firefighter extinguishes the blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Hefty means weighty and large, so the comparative means bigger and weightier.

clue.text: Crook held in gaol in N Sea island

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of shape, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A criminal is locked up in a prison on a North Sea island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' rearranges HELD + IN + GAOL; the second 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This small archipelago off Germany's coast lies in the North Sea.

clue.text: Food put in the meadows for the birds

indicators.note: put in signals that the food word is placed inside the meadows word

parts.note: meadows are grassy fields
fare is food and drink provided

explanation.surface: Someone scatters food in the fields to feed the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is the container signal; the bird is a large thrush that winters in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large thrushes that winter in Britain, so they are birds.

clue.text: They're Berber musical phrases

explanation.surface: North African tribesmen are known for their melodies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rif people of northern Morocco are a Berber group; and short repeated patterns in jazz or rock are melodic phrases.

clue.text: New crusade for an old vehicle

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of crusade are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh campaign is launched to save an ancient vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-hand automobile has had previous owners, so it is not brand new.

clue.text: Unqualified to make a statement

explanation.surface: Someone without credentials speaks up anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Total or absolute means complete, without reservation; and to say something aloud is to speak words.

clue.text: The third half?

parts.note: read as arithmetic, half of one third is a fraction one part in six

explanation.definitionFit: Halving a third gives one part of six equal parts.

clue.text: Remains of a general

explanation.surface: What is left of a military commander after battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment that remains in wine; and the possessive of Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general, sounds the same.

clue.text: Overtake father by boat

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
SS stands for steamship, a boat

explanation.surface: A dad overtakes someone while travelling by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by or move ahead of another vehicle is to overtake it.

clue.text: Going with some hesitation to make a bid

parts.note: off means going away, departing
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly puts in a bid at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose a price is to tender, putting money forward.

clue.text: No way to get wealthy ——you'll just get the bird

parts.note: O represents zero, nothing
St is short for street, a way
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: There is no road to riches: all you get is mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' is an idiom for being jeered at, which hides the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This large flightless African runner is the biggest living bird.

clue.text: Go back to the nunnery

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws to the convent.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to move back; and a secluded religious house is a place of seclusion for nuns or monks.

clue.text: She's worshipped by a man in the gallery

indicators.note: in signals that the man's name is placed inside the gallery word

parts.note: the gods are the highest gallery seats in a theatre
Des is a man's name, short for Desmond

explanation.surface: A woman is adored by a fellow sitting up in the theatre gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres 'the gods' are the cheapest, highest gallery seats; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A female deity is a divine woman who is adored and prayed to.

clue.text: One in unusual stress doesn't give in

indicators.note: in signals that the letter for one goes inside the rearranged letters
unusual suggests the letters of stress appear in an odd new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone under unusual pressure refuses to yield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges STRESS to RESSTS; 'in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand or oppose is to hold firm and not yield.

clue.text: Operatic heroine that is at heart betrayed

indicators.note: at heart signals that the betrayal word sits in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
sold means betrayed, as in sold out

explanation.surface: An opera heroine is betrayed in her heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' puts SOLD in the middle of IE.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Irish princess of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde, an opera's leading lady.

clue.text: Go-ahead newspaper article?

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs an enterprising piece.
explanation.definitionFit: One who goes ahead heads the field; and an editorial in a paper is its principal opinion article.

clue.text: Leaf pattern jumper

indicators.note: pattern as a verb suggests the letters of leaf are arranged in a new design

explanation.surface: A sweater knitted with a leaf design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pattern' rearranges LEAF; 'jumper' is a British sweater in the surface but here an insect that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny parasitic insect is famous for leaping great distances.

clue.text: Limits one's ambitions

explanation.surface: Someone sets bounds on what they hope for.
explanation.definitionFit: Boundaries are extremities or limits; and aims or goals are what a person strives toward.

clue.text: Unhealthy antagonism?

parts.note: read literally, a sick sensation in the body; read idiomatically, hostility or resentment

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means resentment or hostility, and literally a sensation of sickness.

clue.text: A boy of the present time

explanation.surface: A lad of today.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a boy's given name; and Christmas is the season of gifts, a present-giving time.

clue.text: A flower will transform these areas

indicators.note: will transform suggests the letters of these and areas are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Planting a flower will change the look of these spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the wild pansy, a small violet-family bloom.
